survey: A folding camp chair stands on a tabletop, seen from above and in front, with its front-right corner closest to the viewer. Seat: a green canvas panel stretched between a front tube and the back frame. The front tube runs left to right and falls slightly toward the right. The seat top shows as a narrow plane, which fits a seat that sits close to eye level. Back: a rectangular tube frame holding a green canvas panel with a tent-and-campfire emblem. Its uprights are close to vertical, and its top bar rises slightly to the right. Legs: one X-shaped pair of tubes on each side, joined by a pivot bolt. At seat height each back upright bends into a diagonal leg that runs down to a front foot. The other tube of each X runs from the front corner of the seat to a back foot. Feet: two foot bars with rubber caps, at front and back, sit on the tabletop and outline a four-sided footprint seen from well above. The left and right X frames mirror each other. Edges that run across the chair (seat front tube, back top bar, foot bars) all slope toward one shared vanishing point far to the left. That puts eye level at about the top of the backrest canvas. Edges that run front to back (the sides of the seat and the footprint) rise loosely toward one point to the right. The seat looks flat and the footprint looks open, which is right for their heights below eye level. The tabletop's back edge is close to level, which fits a table turned at a different angle from the chair. All four feet sit on the drawn floor plane, and the shadow falls onto that same plane.
